baseline: Host LTP 20260529 on Linux 6.8.0-124-generic: 5 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken. Setup installs SIG_IGN for SIGXFSZ, sets RLIMIT_FSIZE cur=max=2*BUFSIZ=16384, opens tmp_file O_RDWR|O_CREAT and writes BUFSIZ=8192 bytes (file size 8192, offset 8192). Per assertion: (1) llseek01.c:30 lseek(fd, 80*BUFSIZ=655360, SEEK_SET) returns 655360 - seeking past RLIMIT_FSIZE is always legal, lseek never consults the limit; (2) llseek01.c:36 write(fd, buf, 8192) at offset 655360 returns -1/EFBIG because the start offset is already >= the 16384 limit, and SIGXFSZ is raised (ignored here); (3) llseek01.c:41 lseek(fd, 8192, SEEK_SET) returns 8192; (4) llseek01.c:47 write(fd, buf, 8192) at offset 8192 returns 8192 - the start offset 8192 is strictly below the limit, so the write is permitted and clamped to min(8192, 16384-8192)=8192, i.e. it completes in full and lands exactly on the limit with no signal; (5) llseek01.c:52 write(fd, buf, 8192) now at offset 16384 returns -1/EFBIG, since offset == limit counts as at-or-past. The governing rule is a comparison against the *start* offset, not against offset+count.
failing_assertion: llseek01.c:36-39 `if (write(fildes, write_buff, BUFSIZ) == -1)` - Asterinas's write() returns 8192 (success) at offset 655360 instead of -1/EFBIG, so the else branch runs `tst_brk(TFAIL, "write successful after file size limit")`. tst_brk aborts the whole test_all, so assertions 3-5 never execute. qemu.log line 43 `llseek01: fail (0.014s)`, kirk summary Passed: 1 / Failed: 1 (only assertion 1 at llseek01.c:32 ran and passed), versus host 5/0.
root_cause: RLIMIT_FSIZE is simply never consulted on any write path. `grep -rn FSIZE kernel/src/` returns exactly two enforcement sites - kernel/src/syscall/truncate.rs:56 (check_length, shared by sys_truncate and sys_ftruncate) and kernel/src/syscall/fallocate.rs:55 (check_offset_and_len) - and zero hits anywhere under kernel/src/fs/. So the file-extending write path is unguarded end to end: sys_write (kernel/src/syscall/write.rs:21-39) resolves the fd and calls file.write(&mut reader) with no limit check; InodeHandle::write (inode_handle.rs:287-312) checks only Rights::WRITE and O_APPEND, then at line 308 calls file_ops.write_at(*offset, reader, status_flags) with the raw 655360 offset; RamInode::write_at (kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/ramfs/fs.rs:721-756, the fs backing the default /tmp workdir this run used) computes new_size = offset + write_len = 663552, unconditionally sets inode_meta.size = new_size, grows the page cache and returns write_len. The 8192 propagates back up through inode_handle.rs:309 (*offset += len) to SyscallReturn::Return(8192), so write() reports full success. Nothing in that chain reads ctx.process.resource_limits(), and no SIGXFSZ is raised - the only in-tree signal-from-write precedent is the SIGPIPE enqueue at kernel/src/fs/pipe/common.rs:478-487. The pre-existing FIXME at kernel/src/process/rlimit.rs:2 ("The resource limits should be respected by the corresponding subsystems of the kernel") names this class of gap directly.
invariant: A write to a regular file must be bounded by RLIMIT_FSIZE, and the bound is evaluated against the write's starting offset, not its end: if the starting offset is at or beyond the current soft limit the write transfers nothing, fails with EFBIG, and raises SIGXFSZ on the calling thread; if the starting offset is below the limit the write is permitted and its byte count is clamped to (limit - offset), which is an ordinary short write with no signal and no error. Seeking is unaffected - setting a file offset beyond RLIMIT_FSIZE always succeeds, because the limit constrains the bytes a file may hold, not the positions a descriptor may name. A limit of RLIM_INFINITY imposes no bound.
owning_layer: The per-open file-description layer inside the VFS: InodeHandle's FileLike::write / FileLike::write_at in kernel/src/fs/file/inode_handle.rs:287-342, above every concrete filesystem and below every syscall entry. This is Asterinas's closest structural equivalent to Linux's generic_write_checks: it is the single funnel that all five regular-file write entry points reach, it already holds the offset and applies the other per-open write policies (Rights::WRITE, O_APPEND), and both branches it needs are already distinguished there - the !is_offset_aware early returns at lines 295-297 and 275-277 are exactly where pipes and other non-seekable InodeHandles leave, so a check placed after them naturally scopes itself to seekable regular files without a new type test. The limit must NOT be enforced in the individual filesystems (ramfs/ext2/exfat write_at), which are below the point where a process's rlimits are a meaningful input and which are also reached by internal metadata writes that no rlimit governs; nor in kernel/src/syscall/write.rs alone, which is the tempting narrow edit and the one that leaves four other syscalls broken.
linux_reference: fs/read_write.c, generic_write_check_limits() - read from git.kernel.org. It is VFS-side, not filesystem-side and not in mm/filemap.c: `loff_t limit = rlimit(RLIMIT_FSIZE); if (limit != RLIM_INFINITY) { if (pos >= limit) { send_sig(SIGXFSZ, current, 0); return -EFBIG; } *count = min(*count, limit - pos); }`. Note the three details that fix a naive patch: the test is `pos >= limit` on the start offset (so offset == limit is already an error), the signal is sent on the failing path only, and the under-limit case silently clamps rather than erroring. It is reached from generic_write_checks_count -> generic_write_checks, which every regular-file write path calls, and is shared with generic_copy_file_checks (copy_file_range) and generic_remap_checks (clone/dedupe). Linux deliberately does not apply it to pipes, sockets, or mmap stores. Asterinas already mirrors Linux's SIGXFSZ disposition - SigDefaultAction::Core at kernel/src/process/signal/sig_action.rs:150 - and SIGXFSZ = 25 is defined at kernel/src/process/signal/constants.rs:54, so no signal plumbing is missing.
other_callers: Four more syscalls share the defect today, which is what makes the layer choice load-bearing rather than cosmetic. Reaching InodeHandle::write_at: sys_pwrite64 (kernel/src/syscall/pwrite64.rs:35) and do_sys_pwritev (kernel/src/syscall/pwritev.rs:114, in a per-iovec loop that advances cur_offset). Reaching InodeHandle::write: do_sys_writev (kernel/src/syscall/pwritev.rs:161) and sys_sendfile (kernel/src/syscall/sendfile.rs:159, via FileHandle::write_bytes, which is a thin wrapper at kernel/src/fs/file/file_handle.rs:253). memfd inodes also route through ramfs write_at (kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/ramfs/memfd.rs:145) and inherit the same behavior. Every one of these funnels through inode_handle.rs:287-342, so a single check there covers all five; a check in syscall/write.rs would cover one. Deliberately out of scope: pipes and sockets (Linux exempts them, and in Asterinas they exit at the !is_offset_aware early return before any such check), mmap'd stores (Linux does not enforce RLIMIT_FSIZE on page faults either), and the two existing sites in truncate.rs / fallocate.rs, which are already correct for their own syscalls.
suggested_direction: Add a private helper in kernel/src/fs/file/inode_handle.rs that takes the starting offset and the reader's remaining length and returns the permitted length, then call it from InodeHandle::write (after the O_APPEND adjustment at lines 301-306 has settled the real offset, and after the !is_offset_aware early return at 295-297) and from InodeHandle::write_at (likewise after the O_APPEND adjustment at 333-339). Mirror generic_write_check_limits exactly: read ResourceType::RLIMIT_FSIZE via current!().resource_limits() - the fs layer already reaches process state this way, e.g. kernel/src/fs/vfs/path/dentry.rs:472 and kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/procfs/pid/task/stat.rs:249 - short-circuit when the soft limit is RLIM_INFINITY (u64::MAX), return EFBIG when offset >= limit after enqueueing SIGXFSZ on the current thread, and otherwise clamp the transfer to (limit - offset). Copy the SIGXFSZ enqueue shape from kernel/src/fs/pipe/common.rs:478-487 (UserSignal::new(SIGXFSZ, UserSignalKind::Kill, pid, ruid) via posix_thread.enqueue_signal). Clamping is best done by limiting the reader, e.g. reader.limit(permitted), so the short write falls out of the existing `*offset += len` accounting at line 309 with no extra bookkeeping. Three traps to respect: (a) the comparison is on the start offset with >=, not on offset+len - using offset+len > limit would wrongly reject nothing here but would also wrongly *accept* a write starting exactly at the limit, and using offset+len >= limit would break assertion 4, which must succeed in full at offset 8192 landing exactly on 16384; (b) the under-limit path must be a silent short write, not an error, and must not raise SIGXFSZ; (c) do not gate on anything that catches pipes - they must keep returning their current errors, and fsync03's pipe/FIFO behavior committed in run-7UHmXC must stay green. Verify with the default configuration (no CONFORMANCE_TEST_WORKDIR override), since llseek01 comes from all.txt and is enabled by uncommenting its line.
